learningObjectives: Define what a Verification Attribute is.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Scenario: A New SUT Feature to Verify

elements.text: Independent hypothetical requirement: positive quantity 4 should produce a success message, while -4 should produce a defined validation error. Model the expected output in an Attribute with BusinessRelevant = Result and map it to a Verify TestStepValue. The Attribute property alone does not change a TestStepValue’s ActionMode. Review the assertion’s expected text and the actual control/property being verified. This example does not certify the current Demo Web Shop behavior.

Inspect the intended model and data changes. Keep shared Library reuse unless a deliberate local copy is needed. Confirm SchemaName and the TemplateInstance data source rather than assuming a new schema link redirects every existing instance. Inspect all XL paths, map expected output to Verify, and run Check Template. Preserve manual edits and relevant execution evidence before regeneration; deleting the old TemplateInstance is not a universal prerequisite. A TestStepValue can contain a composed expression, so it is not universally limited to one XL reference. When deliberately replacing its mapping, edit the expression and inspect the resulting path.

Create TemplateInstance generates a container of concrete tests. Reinstantiate Instance repeats generation for the selected existing TemplateInstance and needs its data source. It is not a guaranteed additive merge that preserves all manual edits or stale cases. ChangedManually records edits since generation and resets when cases are generated again. Inspect the selected data source, selector and intended generated subset; compare the resulting cases before execution.

Independent practice: add a hypothetical expected login outcome to synthetic user data. Map it to Verify, inspect paths and conditions, regenerate the selected TemplateInstance and trial-run representative cases. Original Academy exercise files and solution workspaces were inaccessible and have not been verified.

examPitfalls.title: Regeneration can affect manual work
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating reinstantiation as a harmless additive refresh.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review manual edits, sources and execution evidence before generation.

examPitfalls.title: Expected data is not an ActionMode
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a Result Attribute alone creates a working assertion.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map expected data to the appropriate Verify value and inspect the control/property.

examPitfalls.title: Source selection must be checked
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a changed Template schema redirects all existing TemplateInstances.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect both the schema and the chosen instance’s data source.

examPitfalls.title: Do not delete as a routine update step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Removing the previous TemplateInstance and its useful history without reviewing the consequences.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Plan regeneration or replacement deliberately and preserve needed work first.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How should a TestCase-Design expected-output Attribute be used in an assertion?

options.text: Treat its icon color as sufficient proof that execution will verify it.
Use it only to rename the Template.
Assume its Character always forces a Failed result.
Set BusinessRelevant to Result where appropriate, map its expected value to Verify, and inspect the assertion.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The expected data must be connected to an actual verification with the intended target.

optionExplanations.A: An icon or data property alone does not establish the execution ActionMode.
optionExplanations.B: Expected output supports an assertion rather than merely object naming.
optionExplanations.C: Character describes input validity, not an automatic execution-failure status.
optionExplanations.D: The expected data must be connected to an actual verification with the intended target.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Before replacing the data source or regenerating an existing TemplateInstance, which preparation is appropriate?

options.text: Inspect the instance’s source and selectors, preserve needed manual edits/evidence, and plan regeneration or replacement deliberately.
Always delete the previous instance without examining its contents.
Only rename the Template.
Convert it back to TestCase as a harmless refresh.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This reviews the intended generation and preserves useful existing work.

optionExplanations.A: This reviews the intended generation and preserves useful existing work.
optionExplanations.B: Deletion can discard useful work/evidence and is not universally required.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming does not review or change the instance data source.
optionExplanations.D: Reverse conversion loses template information instead of harmlessly refreshing it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The linked data combinations changed. How do you regenerate an existing TemplateInstance?

options.text: Assume the existing cases update immediately.
Select the intended TemplateInstance and Reinstantiate, after reviewing its source and manual changes.
Always delete the entire instance as the only supported method.
Hand-create each new case as the only supported method.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The selected existing container is regenerated from its configured source.

optionExplanations.A: Existing generated cases require generation to reflect model/data changes.
optionExplanations.B: The selected existing container is regenerated from its configured source.
optionExplanations.C: Reinstantiate is supported, so deletion is not the only update path.
optionExplanations.D: The documented generation workflow avoids manually rebuilding every combination.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After assigning a TestSheet to a Template, where can you confirm the linked TestCase-Design source type and name?

options.text: Inspect SchemaName in the Template Properties pane.
Assume all existing TemplateInstances now use that source without checking.
Recreate the entire Template to view the name.
Look only at a browser TCP.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: SchemaName identifies the linked TestCase-Design source type and name.

optionExplanations.A: SchemaName identifies the linked TestCase-Design source type and name.
optionExplanations.B: A schema change is not proof that every instance source has changed.
optionExplanations.C: The property can be inspected without rebuilding the model.
optionExplanations.D: Browser TCP selection does not identify the linked TestSheet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestStepValue uses an old Email XL path. You deliberately want a new mapping. What is a controlled change?

options.text: Delete the entire TestStep as a prerequisite.
Assume a drag operation guarantees the intended new semantic mapping.
Rename the TestStepValue and leave its Value unchanged.
Replace the old expression deliberately, inspect the new XL path and recheck the Template.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A deliberate expression change and validation addresses the actual mapping.

optionExplanations.A: The expression can be edited without removing the whole step.
optionExplanations.B: Generated or dragged paths still need semantic inspection.
optionExplanations.C: Changing the name alone leaves the old Value expression intact.
optionExplanations.D: A deliberate expression change and validation addresses the actual mapping.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the documented direction for linking a TestSheet to a Template?

options.text: Right click on the Template, select Instantiation, choose the TestSheet.
Drag and drop the TestSheet onto the Template.
Right click on the TestSheet and select the correct Template from the list.
Drag the TestSheet and drop it onto the TemplateInstances.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Drop the TestSheet directly onto the Template to link the data source.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented TestSheet-to-Template assignment operation.
optionExplanations.B: Drop the TestSheet directly onto the Template to link the data source.
optionExplanations.C: The described reverse-side menu is not this documented procedure.
optionExplanations.D: The target in this schema-assignment procedure is the Template itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the normal Template generation workflow, why create a TemplateInstance?

options.text: No, I can link a Template to an ExecutionList and the {XL[ ]} References are translated during runtime.
To generate concrete TestCases from the model and its selected data.
Yes, because you link the Template to a TestSheet during Instantiation.
No, this is done automatically by Tosca during runtime.

practiceQuiz.hint: Inspect the documented model, data source and generation step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The TemplateInstance contains the generated concrete tests.

optionExplanations.A: The stated model-generation workflow creates concrete tests before execution.
optionExplanations.B: The TemplateInstance contains the generated concrete tests.
optionExplanations.C: Schema linking and instantiation are distinct operations.
optionExplanations.D: Generation is an explicit model operation, not guaranteed at runtime.
